newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Independent seeks rest of W&H.
newsitem.headline: Independent seeks rest of W&H.

text.p: Independent Press Communications said on Monday it intended to offer NZ$10.50/share to purchase all outstanding shares in New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton Ltd.
Independent said it was making both a written offer and a stand in the market on the New Zealand Stock Exchange, and shareholders could accept either.
Under the written offer, W&H shareholders may receive either NZ$10.50 cash, or use some or all of this cash entitlement to acquire cumulative exchangeable preference shares.
These will be allotted at the rate of one for every $8 of the cash to which shareholders would otherwise have been entitled.
Independent will issue up to NZ$320 million of exchangeable shares on a first come first served basis.
The exchangeable shares will be entitled to a five percent dividend yield which is expected to carry full imputation credits.

At the option of the holder, these shares will in seven years time be either exchangeable into ordinary shares in Independent Newspapers PLC on a one-for-one basis, or redeemable in cash at their full $8 face value.
The offer is by Independent Press Communications (IPCL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Independent Newspapers Plc (INP). INP owns half of three companies which collectively own 45.15 percent of W&H.

INP Deputy Chairman John Meagher said: "A successful offer will further broaden and develop the international composition of the INP Group and its leading positions in newspaper publishing. INP continues to be particularly attracted to the stable and progressive economic environment which New Zealand has to offer."
Wilson and Horton closed on Monday at $9.70.
IPCL expects to commence its stand-in-the-market offer on or shortly after October 8. Written offer documents will be sent about October 5.
INP said it would apply for permission to list the exchangeable shares on the New Zealand Stock Exchange and also intends to apply for an additional listing of its own ordinary shares on the NZSE.
